name: Low beta to the equal-weight crypto index (ex self), bottom half, 70th-percentile hold buffer
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. For symbol s, index return on bar k = mean of ret(b,k) over all other symbols in the view with L >= need. beta_s = cov(ret_s, index)/var(index) over the last window bars ending at e (sample). Rank ascending by beta; percentile p_s = (position-1)/(n-1). Hold set H (ctx.state, starts empty): keep s in H if p_s <= holdPct; add symbols in ascending beta order until |H| = ceil(selectPct * n). Weights: equal over H. ew if n < minNames; reset H to empty then. n = number of scored symbols (BTC included). Symbols in H that are no longer scored are removed first. If |H| already >= ceil(selectPct*n) nothing is added and nothing beyond the holdPct test is removed.
rationale: If the premium is about market beta it should not depend on BTC being the reference asset; the buffer makes the test cost-aware by stopping names from churning on small rank changes.
source: Frazzini & Pedersen 2014 JFE; Novy-Marx & Velikov 2016 RFS (buffer rules)

name: Low correlation with BTC only (beta with the volatility ratio stripped out), rank-weighted
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret_s and ret_BTC over the last window bars ending at e. BTCUSDT corr = 1. rank-weight(rows asc by score) : symbol at position q (1 = highest score = highest beta) gets weight q / (n(n+1)/2) so the lowest-score name has the largest weight (Frazzini-Pedersen rank construction, long-only, BTC included with its own score). applied to corr (lowest correlation gets the largest weight). ew if fewer than minNames symbols scored.
rationale: Beta = correlation x sigma_s/sigma_BTC, so a low-beta sort can be a low-volatility sort in disguise; ranking on correlation alone asks whether the co-movement component carries the effect.
source: Frazzini & Pedersen 2014 JFE section 3 decomposition; Blitz, van Vliet & Baltussen 2020 (low-vol vs low-beta)

name: Low BTC-beta picked only inside the high-volatility half
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. beta(sym, W) = cov(ret_sym, ret_ref over the last W bars ending at e, aligned by bar index from the end) / var(ret_ref); both sample (W-1). Reference = BTCUSDT unless stated. vol_s = sample std of ret_s over the last window bars. Exclude BTCUSDT from the sort. Keep the ceil(volHalf*n) symbols with the HIGHEST vol; within that set take the pick lowest-beta symbols. Weights: 1/(pick+1) each plus 1/(pick+1) in BTCUSDT (mirrors r25-crypto-btcbeta-low). ew if fewer than minNames symbols scored or fewer than pick in the high-vol half. Here n = number of scored symbols excluding BTCUSDT; minNames applies to that n.
rationale: If low beta still earns a premium among the most volatile coins, the leaders are not a low-volatility anomaly relabelled; if it vanishes the earlier result was volatility.
source: Blitz, van Vliet & Baltussen 2020 Journal of Portfolio Management (volatility effect vs beta effect)

name: Rank-weighted low BTC-beta scaled by a BTC trend grid
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. beta(sym, W) = cov(ret_sym, ret_ref over the last W bars ending at e, aligned by bar index from the end) / var(ret_ref); both sample (W-1). Reference = BTCUSDT unless stated. rank-weight(rows asc by score) : symbol at position q (1 = highest score = highest beta) gets weight q / (n(n+1)/2) so the lowest-score name has the largest weight (Frazzini-Pedersen rank construction, long-only, BTC included with its own score). on beta_90 exactly as r27-crypto-lowbeta-rankw. trendFrac = (number of W in smaWindows with BTC close[e] > SMA_W of BTC close ending at e) / 3. Final weights = rank weights x trendFrac (remainder cash). ew x trendFrac if fewer than minNames scored.
rationale: The low-beta survivors hold 95-100% gross, so the robustness report notes they are close to buy-and-hold in bear markets; an a-priori trend grid tests whether the selection effect survives once market exposure is cut in downtrends.
source: Frazzini & Pedersen 2014 JFE; Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen 2017 JPM (multi-horizon trend); robustness-0929.md caveat (e)

name: Double sort: bottom-half BTC-beta intersected with top-half 4-week momentum
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. beta(sym, W) = cov(ret_sym, ret_ref over the last W bars ending at e, aligned by bar index from the end) / var(ret_ref); both sample (W-1). Reference = BTCUSDT unless stated. mom_s = b[e].close / b[e - momLookback].close - 1. Over the n scored symbols (BTC included, beta 1): LB = the floor(n/2) lowest-beta names, HM = the ceil(n/2) highest-mom names. H = LB intersect HM. If |H| >= minHold weights are equal over H; otherwise equal over LB. ew if n < minNames.
rationale: Low beta and short-horizon momentum are the two strongest independent crypto findings in the registry; an a-priori intersection asks whether they add or whether one subsumes the other.
source: Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen 2019 (quality/momentum double sorts); Liu & Tsyvinski 2021 RFS

name: Crypto momentum consensus: top half on every horizon of 14/21/28 days
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. For each horizon h rank r_h(s) = b[e].close / b[e-h].close - 1 descending; T_h = the ceil(n/2) highest. H = intersection of T_h over the three horizons. If |H| >= minHold weights are equal over H; otherwise 100% cash (return {}). ew if n < minNames.
rationale: A name that is a momentum winner on every nearby horizon is a cleaner winner than one that tops a single lookback; a consensus filter should lose breadth but gain per-name reliability if the effect is real.
source: Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen 2017 JPM; Jegadeesh & Titman 1993 (robustness to formation period)

name: Crypto momentum with the most recent week skipped (28-7)
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. score(s) = b[e-skip].close / b[e-lookback].close - 1. K = max(3, round(frac*n)). Hold the top K equal weight. ew if n < minNames.
rationale: Equity momentum skips the last month because the most recent return reverses; crypto momentum leaders use the full window, so skipping the last week tests whether the 3-week signal is momentum or just recent-week continuation.
source: Jegadeesh & Titman 1993 JF (12-1 skip); Liu & Tsyvinski 2021 RFS

name: Crypto 3-week momentum, rank weights across the whole cross-section (no top-K cut)
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. score(s) = b[e].close / b[e-lookback].close - 1. Sort descending; position q = 1 for the best. weight_q = (n - q + 1) / (n(n+1)/2) (best gets the largest weight, every name gets some). ew if n < minNames.
rationale: Top-K portfolios depend on a handful of names and on where the cut falls; a rank-weighted version uses the whole cross-section and is the drop-top-asset robustness check built into the construction.
source: Frazzini & Pedersen 2014 JFE (rank weights); Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen 2013 JF

name: Crypto breadth gate with hysteresis: in when 60% of coins are above their 50-day SMA, out at 40%
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. breadth = (count of symbols with L >= need and b[e].close > SMA_50 of close ending at e) / (count with L >= need); if fewer than minCoins symbols have L >= need, breadth is undefined. Undefined breadth -> ew over the view (state unchanged). ctx.state.on (starts false): set true when breadth >= on, false when breadth <= off, otherwise unchanged. Weights: ew over all symbols in the view when state.on, else {} (cash). minNames does not apply to this spec; only the fallbacks stated in this rule are used.
rationale: Market-level breadth is a different information set from each coin's own trend: it is a cross-sectional count that single-asset rules cannot see, and hysteresis makes it cheap to trade.
source: Zweig 1986 'Winning on Wall Street' (breadth thrust); Lo & Hasanhodzic 2010 on hysteresis in technical rules

name: Equal-weight crypto scaled continuously by 50-day breadth, weekly
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. breadth = (count of symbols with L >= need and b[e].close > SMA_50 of close ending at e) / (count with L >= need); if fewer than minCoins symbols have L >= need, breadth is undefined. Undefined breadth -> breadth = 1. Weights: every symbol in the view gets breadth / n; remainder cash. n = number of symbols in the view. minNames does not apply to this spec; only the fallbacks stated in this rule are used.
rationale: A continuous breadth exposure avoids the threshold choice entirely; if the gate in spec 22 works only at 0.6/0.4 and this fails, the gate was tuned.
source: Zweig 1986; Faber 2007 (a quantitative approach to tactical asset allocation)

name: Max of the fear grid and the SMA grid: trend or capitulation, daily
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. Symbols with fewer than `need` bars are not skipped; they use the warm-up trendFrac below. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. fearFrac (market-level): keep ctx.state.last[th] = rebalance index e at which ctx.macro("FNG") <= th was last seen, per threshold th (rank() is called every day because rebalance is daily; ctx.macro returns the value known by the close of that day; null -> not <= th). fearFrac = mean over all (th, H) pairs in thresholds x horizons of [state.last[th] is defined and (current e) - state.last[th] <= H-1]; 0 before any FNG data. k_s = count of W in windows with b[e].close > mean of close over the last W bars ending at e; trendFrac_s = k_s/10; trendFrac_s = 1 if the symbol has L < need (warm-up). weight_s = max(fearFrac, trendFrac_s) / n; remainder cash. n = number of symbols in the view. minNames does not apply to this spec; only the fallbacks stated in this rule are used.
rationale: The leader's 'trend OR fear' logic with both legs replaced by fixed grids; if this is weaker than the point-estimate leader the leader was fitted, if similar the logic is robust.
source: Antoniou, Doukas & Subrahmanyam 2013 JFQA; r27-cx-tsmom28-fngfear

name: Equal-weight ensemble of the three crypto leader families, weekly
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. low-beta leg: rank weights (rank-weight(rows asc by score) : symbol at position q (1 = highest score = highest beta) gets weight q / (n(n+1)/2) so the lowest-score name has the largest weight (Frazzini-Pedersen rank construction, long-only, BTC included with its own score).) on beta_90 vs BTC (BTC beta 1), ew if < 8 names. momentum leg: top max(3, round(0.3n)) by 21-day return, equal weight, ew if < 8 names. trend leg: per-coin (k/4)/n where k = number of W in [20,50,100,200] with close > SMA_W (1/n during warm-up). Final weight_s = (lowbeta_s + momentum_s + trend_s)/3. The low-beta and momentum legs score only symbols with L >= need (n = that count, ew over the view if < 8); the trend leg covers every symbol in the view (n = view count) with 1/n for L < need.
rationale: Three a-priori independent signals (beta, cross-sectional momentum, own trend) averaged with no weights to fit is the standard robust-portfolio construction; a diversified ensemble that keeps the excess while cutting maxDD is what the registry's single-signal leaders cannot show.
source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen 2013 JF (value and momentum everywhere: combination portfolios); DeMiguel, Garlappi & Uppal 2009 RFS (1/N)

name: Sector momentum, rank averaged over 3/6/12 months, top 3, own-trend gate to IEF
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. For each sector with L >= need: score = mean over h of the cross-sectional percentile rank of b[e].close/b[e-h].close - 1. Top-3 (= top) by score each get 1/top, but a chosen sector whose own b[e].close/b[e-gate].close - 1 <= 0 has its 1/top moved to IEF. If fewer than 6 sectors have history -> ew over the view. IEF is never scored; it only receives gated weight. Percentile rank in [0,1], 1 = best return. minNames does not apply to this spec; only the fallbacks stated in this rule are used.
rationale: Sector rotation in the registry used single lookbacks (1m, 6m, 12m) with mixed results; a fixed rank blend plus the dual-momentum absolute gate is the Antonacci construction that practitioners actually run.
source: Antonacci 2014 'Dual Momentum Investing'; Moskowitz & Grinblatt 1999 JF (industry momentum)

name: Sector breadth gate with hysteresis (60% above 200-day in, 40% out), else IEF, weekly
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. Sectors = the 11 symbols in the view other than IEF (XLC only from its listing). m = number of sectors with L >= need. breadth = (count of those m with b[e].close > SMA_200 of close ending at e) / m; undefined if m < 6. Undefined breadth -> ew over the view (state unchanged). ctx.state.on (starts false): true when breadth >= on, false when <= off, else unchanged. on -> 1/m to each of the m sectors with L >= need (IEF 0); off -> {IEF: 1}. minNames does not apply to this spec; only the fallbacks stated in this rule are used.
rationale: The registry tested a 50% breadth gate on individual stocks weekly; sector breadth with hysteresis is the version that institutional tactical allocators quote, and it is testable on ETF data with IEF as the risk-off leg.
source: Zweig 1986; Faber 2007; breadth-pct200-timing-gate (stock version)

name: 12-1 momentum top 15% only when market breadth (% above 200-day) is at least 50%
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. breadth = fraction of stocks with L >= need whose b[e].close > SMA_200. If breadth < breadthMin return {} (cash). Otherwise top round(frac*n) by 12-1 score, equal weight. ew if n < minNames.
rationale: Momentum crashes happen when the market rebounds from a broad decline (Daniel-Moskowitz); gating on breadth, a market-state variable, is the simplest crash-avoidance rule and uses no momentum-specific tuning.
source: Daniel & Moskowitz 2016 JFE (momentum crashes); Cooper, Gutierrez & Hameed 2004 JF (market states and momentum)

name: Composite momentum: average rank of 12-1, 6-1 and distance to 52-week high, top 15%
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. For each stock: a = b[e-skip].close/b[e-long].close - 1; c = b[e-skip].close/b[e-short].close - 1; h = b[e].close / max high over the last highWindow bars. score = mean of the three cross-sectional percentile ranks. Top round(frac*n), equal weight. ew if n < minNames.
rationale: George & Hwang show 52-week-high proximity and past-return momentum are distinct signals; a fixed three-signal composite is more diversified than any one and is what quant long-only funds actually run.
source: George & Hwang 2004 JF (52-week high); Jegadeesh & Titman 1993 JF; Asness et al. 2013 JF

name: Monthly 200-day SMA check: hold each coin above its 200-day average, checked only at month-end
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. For each symbol with L >= need: weight = 1/n if b[e].close > mean close over the last sma bars, else 0. Symbols with L < need get 1/n. Remainder cash. n = number of symbols in the view. minNames does not apply to this spec; only the fallbacks stated in this rule are used.
rationale: The most widely quoted retail crypto rule ('above the 200-day on the monthly close') has only been tested daily in the registry; monthly checking is both the cost-aware and the as-practised version.
source: Faber 2007 (10-month SMA, monthly check); Zakamulin 2017

name: 12-1 momentum top 15% with a 10% basket drawdown circuit breaker (cash for the next month)
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. Target basket T = top round(frac*n) by 12-1 score. basketRet_k = equal-weight daily return of the names held at the previous rebalance (ctx.state.prev) over the last ddWindow bars; P_0 = 1, P_j = product of (1+basketRet) over the first j of those ddWindow bars; dd = 1 - P_last / max(P_0..P_last). If ctx.state.prev is defined and dd >= ddTrigger return {} (cash) and keep state.prev = T; otherwise equal weight over T and state.prev = T. ew if n < minNames. Names in state.prev with no bar on a day are left out of that day's mean.
rationale: Daniel-Moskowitz momentum crashes are concentrated in a few months after sharp drawdowns; a pre-set drawdown breaker on the held basket is the risk-management overlay that managed-momentum funds use and that the 12-1 leader lacks.
source: Daniel & Moskowitz 2016 JFE; Barroso & Santa-Clara 2015 JFE

name: Equal-weight crypto basket gated by BTC's own SMA grid (market-level trend only)
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. frac = (count of W in windows with BTCUSDT b[e].close > BTC SMA_W)/10 (1 if BTC has L < need). Every symbol in the view gets frac / n; remainder cash. n = number of symbols in the view. minNames does not apply to this spec; only the fallbacks stated in this rule are used.
rationale: If a market-level BTC trend signal applied to all coins matches the per-coin grid of spec 17, the crypto trend effect is a single market factor and per-coin signals are noise; if it is weaker, coin-level trend carries information.
source: Liu & Tsyvinski 2021 RFS (crypto market factor); Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen 2017 JPM

name: Sector momentum top 3 (6 months) gated by sector breadth hysteresis, else IEF
rule: Portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx). L = bars.length for a symbol, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view, the rebalance-day close). ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1. A symbol with fewer bars than `need` is skipped. If fewer than minNames symbols qualify, return equal weight over every symbol in the view (ew). Ties broken by symbol name ascending. Weights sum to <= 1; unlisted symbols = 0. Sectors = the 11 symbols in the view other than IEF (XLC only from its listing). m = number of sectors with L >= need. breadth = (count of those m with b[e].close > SMA_200 of close ending at e) / m; undefined if m < 6. ctx.state.on (starts false): true when breadth >= on, false when breadth <= off, else unchanged (evaluated at each monthly rebalance). Undefined breadth -> ew over the view (state unchanged). If state.on: top-3 sectors (IEF excluded, L >= lookback+1) by b[e].close/b[e-lookback].close - 1, 1/3 each. Else {IEF: 1}. minNames does not apply to this spec; only the fallbacks stated in this rule are used.
rationale: Combines the two ETF overlays with the fewest free parameters (sector momentum, breadth gate) into the rotation-with-risk-off rule tactical managers actually describe; both parts are fixed from their standalone specs.
source: Antonacci 2014; Zweig 1986; Moskowitz & Grinblatt 1999 JF
